ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The following graphs show the permeability of ions during an action potential in a ventricular contractile cardiac fiber. Based on the graphs, approximately how long does an action potential last in cardiac fibers?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The following graphs show the permeability of ions during an action potential in a ventricular contractile cardiac fiber. Based on the graphs, approximately how long does an action potential last in cardiac fibers?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left graph shows the membrane potential of a ventricular contractile cardiac fiber changing over time, the x-axis is Time (sec), the curve rises rapidly near 0 s, then maintains a relatively long plateau phase, and afterward repolarizes at around about 0.30 s and returns to near the resting potential. The right graph shows the relative permeability of ions such as Na+, Ca2+, K+ changing over time, also covering the same time range. Reasoning: The question asks how long one action potential of a cardiac muscle fiber lasts, so the time interval from the start of rapid depolarization to repolarization returning to near baseline should be read from the left action potential curve. This interval is about from 0 s to 0.30 s, so the duration of the action potential is about 0.30 seconds.

Measure the interval on the x-axis from the beginning of the upstroke to the return near baseline; this is approximately 0.30 seconds.
